Proposition

1. ch3:3.23Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, and let $p\in M$. Every $v\in T_pM$ is the velocity of a smooth curve in $M$.

Proof

\sketch Choose coordinates centered at $p$ and write $v=v^i\partial /\partial x^i|_p$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon >0$, use the coordinate curve

\[ \gamma (t)=(tv^1,\ldots ,tv^n). \tag {3.14} \]

At an interior point its domain is $(-\varepsilon ,\varepsilon )$. At a boundary point, take this domain when $v^n=0$, $[0,\varepsilon )$ when $v^n>0$, and $(-\varepsilon ,0]$ when $v^n<0$. In every case $\gamma (0)=p$ and $\gamma '(0)=v$.
